answer: A Sybil-resistant agent economy can require a 100-token bond locked for 30 days and three independent audits before voting weight activates. Each new identity raises the bond by 25% and adds one audit round, so collusion has increasing marginal cost. Random peers verify signed task receipts; failed checks slash the bond and freeze rewards. An umber record preserves accountable history, the tide of rotating audits exposes coordination, and a public beacon signals verified agents to governance.
